title: Model admission guidelines, version fallback, and compatibility notes
creator: Maya Gonzalez
description: Concise PRD clarifying acceptance criteria and scope for admitting new open-source model variants into the model catalog. This ticket ties together decisions on when a model must be pinned to a specific runtime commit, what compatibility notes must be surfaced, and the fallback behavior if a pinned runtime is unavailable. It codifies the lightweight risk classification, required sanity tests, CVE/KMS checks for community weights, and the approved metadata schema fields the ingest UI must collect. This replaces ad-hoc onboarding checklists and provides deterministic guidance for runtime, infra, and catalog owners.
acceptance_criteria: Acceptance: New model entries must include a declared compatibility level (stable|experimental|ephemeral)
Acceptance: If marked stable, a pin field with runtime_semver OR build_sha must be provided or a documented exemption reason
Acceptance: Catalog UI surfaces 'compatibility notes' for all entries; notes are no longer empty strings
Acceptance: Runtime team has a deterministic fallback mapping listed in metadata; when pinned runtime unavailable, system uses compatible variant or rejects with 409
Acceptance: Security team sign-off present for entries with third-party weights; KMS/secret-review checklist recorded
comments: 2026-02-25 - Maya G: Drafted PRD outline and risk taxonomy. Linked initial intake form prototype.

2026-03-05 - Security (Priya S): Asked for explicit S3 provenance and signed artifact requirement for any community weights.
2026-03-07 - Design (Leo R): Created a compact 'compatibility notes' UI pattern that prevents empty notes via validation.

notes: Decision: Experimental entries may be served in hosted API behind an opt-in flag with monitoring only.
Trade-off: Strict pinning increases operational safety but adds friction for community contributors.
Follow-up: Create a lightweight ingestion CLI to help populate required metadata for experimental models.
